The MUSIC algorithm is a signal processing technique used to estimate the direction of arrival (DOA) of signals in a sensor array.
Ordinary MUSIC algorithms assume that the signals from multiple damage sources are independent.
The proposed correlated 2D-MUSIC method uses spatial smoothing to separate the sensor array into subarrays.
The near-field condition is when the distance between the sensor array and the damage source is small enough that the wave fronts are spherical, not planar.
The wavelength of the signal used in the experiment is 28.7 mm.
The near-field condition for the experiment is when the distance between the ULSA and the damage source is less than or equal to 250.8 mm.
The damage is simulated using a mass block with a 10 mm diameter circular section.
7 PZT sensors are used in the experiment.
The sampling rate used in the experiment is 5 MHz.
The exciting frequency used in the experiment is 50 kHz.
The phase velocity of the signal used in the experiment is 1437 m/s.
The proposed method is validated using experiments on a carbon fiber composite plate and a real aircraft composite oil tank.
The algorithm is able to detect multiple damage sources in the near-field condition.
The spatial smoothing technique is used to separate the sensor array into subarrays.
The correlated 2D-MUSIC method is able to estimate the signal source direction correctly even when the sources are correlated.
